# Overview

This notebook performs quality control checks on the RDA models from Notebook 09, specifically: 1. **Document VIF Threshold Explicitly** - Show VIF computation with defined thresholds 2. **Display and Document VIF Results** - Show which variables passed/failed VIF screening 3. **Generate Methods Text** - Create manuscript-ready language for multiple comparison acknowledgment

## Source the external variables and base data from Notebook 09

```{r}
# Loading data (same as Notebook 09)
base <- read_excel("../data/pig_alr.xlsx")

baseD <- read_excel("../data/diatom_filtered.xlsx") 
baseD <- as.data.frame(cbind("age"= baseD$mean_VT22, scale(baseD[,3:18])))

ext_all <- read_excel("../data/External_forRDA_pig.xlsx")
Names  <- colnames(ext_all)
colnames(ext_all) <- c("age",Names[2:length(Names)])

ext_dia <- read_excel("../data/External_forRDA_dia.xlsx")
Names  <- colnames(ext_dia)
colnames(ext_dia) <- c("age",Names[2:length(Names)])

ext <- ext_all
# REMOVE MEERFELDEMAAR POLLEN: Keep only Holzmaar pollen (HZM), exclude Meerfeldemaar pollen (Mer)
ext_all <- select(ext_all, 1:17) # age + env vars + Holzmaar pollen (NO Meerfeldemaar)
ext_dia <- select(ext_dia, 1:17) # same for diatom dataset

ext_rex <- read_excel("../data/External_forRDA_pig_redox.xlsx")
Names  <- colnames(ext_rex)
colnames(ext_rex) <- c("age",Names[2:length(Names)])
ext_red <- select(ext_rex, 1:26) # redox variables and Holzmaar pollen (NO Meerfeldemaar)
```

## Prepare datasets (same as Notebook 09)

```{r}
ProducerG <-  read_excel("../data/pig_alr_clust.xlsx")
ProdG <- select(ProducerG, 23, 24, 25)

# Use hclust with ward.D2 (replaces rioja's chclust)
clust <- hclust(dist(ProdG, method="euclidean"), method="ward.D2") 
clustercut<-cbind(1:94,cutree(clust,3)) 
ProdG <- bind_cols(ProducerG[,2] , ProdG, clustercut) 
colnames(ProdG)[5] <- 'orderCONISS' 
colnames(ProdG)[6] <- 'CONISScluster'

ProdG_cl <- select(ProdG, 1, 6)

# Prepare all datasets
groups <- read_excel("../data/Pig_clustered_PC.xlsx")
groups <- groups%>% mutate(PZn = case_when(PolZ == "Pleniglacial" ~ "1",
                           PolZ == "Bølling" ~ "2",
                           PolZ == "Allerød" ~ "3",
                           PolZ == "YoungerDryas" ~ "4"))
groups <- select(groups, 2, 23)
colnames(groups) <- c("age","PolZ")
groups <- merge(groups, ProdG_cl)

cleaning_full <-  merge(base, ext, by = "age", all = T)
cleaning_full <- merge(groups, cleaning_full, by = "age", all = T)

cleaning <- merge(base, ext_all, by = "age", all = T)
cleaning <- merge(groups, cleaning, by = "age", all = T)

cleaningRed <- merge(base, ext_red, by = "age", all = T)
cleaningRed <- merge(groups, cleaningRed, by = "age", all = T)

# Remove NaNs
clean <- na.omit(cleaning)
cleanRed <- na.omit(cleaningRed)

# Extract components (columns 5-24 contain all 20 pigments; columns 1-4 are metadata)
base_cl <- select(clean, 5:24)
ext_cl <- select(clean, 25:ncol(clean))

base_cl_rex <- select(cleanRed, 5:24)
ext_cl_rex <- select(cleanRed, 25:ncol(cleanRed))


# Prepare BAY dataset
cleanBAY <- filter(cleaning_full, between(age, 12607, 14200 ))
base_cl_BAY <- select(cleanBAY, 5:24)
ext_cl_BAY <- select(cleanBAY, 24:43)

# Variable reduction (same as Notebook 09)
ext_cl_red <- select(ext_cl, 1:3, 6:15)
ext_cl_red2 <- select(ext_cl, 1:10)
ext_cl_red_BAY <- select(ext_cl_BAY, 1:10, 17:19)
```

# STEP 1: Document VIF Threshold Explicitly

## Define VIF Thresholds

```{r}
# ============================================================
# VIF (Variance Inflation Factor) Thresholds
# ============================================================
# 
# VIF measures how much the variance of a regression coefficient 
# increases due to multicollinearity among predictors.
# 
# General guidelines:
#   - VIF = 1: No correlation with other variables
#   - VIF < 5: Generally acceptable
#   - VIF < 10: Acceptable for exploratory analysis (paleolimnology)
#   - VIF > 10: High multicollinearity; remove variable
#   - VIF > 5-10: Borderline; consider removing based on field knowledge
# 
# For this analysis, we use: VIF_THRESHOLD = 10
# Variables exceeding this threshold will be flagged for removal.

VIF_THRESHOLD <- 10
VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD <- 5

cat("\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("VIF ASSESSMENT PROTOCOL\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Critical Threshold (REMOVE):  VIF > %.1f\n", VIF_THRESHOLD))
cat(sprintf("Caution Threshold (REVIEW):   VIF > %.1f\n", VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD))
cat("Reference: Paleoecological RDA best practices\n")
cat("========================================\n\n")
```

# STEP 2: Display and Document VIF Results

## 2.0 INITIAL ASSESSMENT: Full 16-Variable External Dataset

```{r}
# First, let's check VIFs on the FULL external dataset (16 variables)
# before any reduction is done
rda_model_pig_full_initial <- rda(base_cl ~ ., data= ext_cl, scale=T)

cat("\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("INITIAL VIF CHECK: Pigments with ALL 16 External Variables\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("Response: Pigment data (20 variables)\n")
cat("Predictors: FULL external dataset (16 variables) - BEFORE reduction\n")
cat("\n")

vif_full_initial <- vif.cca(rda_model_pig_full_initial)

vif_full_initial_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(vif_full_initial),
  VIF = round(vif_full_initial, 3),
  Status = ifelse(vif_full_initial > VIF_THRESHOLD, "❌ REMOVE", 
                  ifelse(vif_full_initial > VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD, "⚠️  CAUTION", "✓ OK"))
)

kable(vif_full_initial_df, 
      caption = "Initial VIF Results - Full 16-Variable External Dataset",
      format = "html",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

vif_max_full_initial <- max(vif_full_initial, na.rm = TRUE)
vif_mean_full_initial <- mean(vif_full_initial, na.rm = TRUE)
vars_exceed_full_initial <- sum(vif_full_initial > VIF_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE)
vars_caution_full_initial <- sum(vif_full_initial > VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD & vif_full_initial <= VIF_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("Summary for Full 16-Variable Dataset (BEFORE reduction):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  - Maximum VIF: %.3f\n", vif_max_full_initial))
cat(sprintf("  - Mean VIF: %.3f\n", vif_mean_full_initial))
cat(sprintf("  - Variables exceeding threshold (>%g): %d\n", VIF_THRESHOLD, vars_exceed_full_initial))
cat(sprintf("  - Variables in caution zone (>%g-%g): %d\n", VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD, VIF_THRESHOLD, vars_caution_full_initial))
cat(sprintf("  - Assessment: %s\n\n", 
            ifelse(vars_exceed_full_initial > 0, 
                   "❌ PROBLEMATIC - Variables need to be removed", 
                   "✓ ACCEPTABLE")))

# Identify problematic variables
if (vars_exceed_full_initial > 0) {
  problem_vars <- names(vif_full_initial)[vif_full_initial > VIF_THRESHOLD]
  cat(sprintf("Variables exceeding VIF > %g:\n", VIF_THRESHOLD))
  for (var in problem_vars) {
    cat(sprintf("  - %s (VIF = %.3f)\n", var, vif_full_initial[var]))
  }
  cat("\nThese variables show high multicollinearity and were removed in subsequent analyses.\n\n")
}
```

## 2.1 RDA Model 1: Pigments with Reduced External Variables

```{r}
# Recreate RDA models from Notebook 09 - now with REDUCED variables

kable(vif_pig_df,

vif_mean_pig <- mean(vif_pig, na.rm = TRUE)
vars_exceed_pig <- sum(vif_pig > VIF_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE)
vars_caution_pig <- sum(vif_pig > VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD & vif_pig <= VIF_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\n")

cat(sprintf("  - Mean VIF: %.3f\n", vif_mean_pig))
cat(sprintf("  - Variables exceeding threshold (>%g): %d\n", VIF_THRESHOLD, vars_exceed_pig))
cat(sprintf("  - Variables in caution zone (>%g-%g): %d\n", VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD, VIF_THRESHOLD, vars_caution_pig))
cat(sprintf("  - Assessment: %s\n\n", 
            ifelse(vars_exceed_pig > 0, "❌ PROBLEMATIC", "✓ ACCEPTABLE")))
```

## 2.4 VALIDATION: VIF-Based Automatic Selection vs. Your Expert Selection

```{r}
cat("\n")
cat("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║  VALIDATION: Automated VIF Selection vs Expert Selection  ║\n")
cat("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

cat("This section tests whether your manual selection of 10 variables\n")
cat("aligns with what a pure VIF-based criterion would select.\n\n")

# --- STEP 1: VIF-BASED AUTOMATIC SELECTION ---

cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("STEP 1: Automated VIF-Based Variable Selection\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("Starting with: Full 16-variable dataset (ext_cl)\n\n")

# Get VIF for full 16-variable model
rda_full_16 <- rda(base_cl ~ ., data = ext_cl, scale = TRUE)
vif_full_16 <- vif.cca(rda_full_16)

cat("VIF values for all 16 variables:\n")
print(round(vif_full_16, 3))
cat("\n")

# Identify variables to remove based on VIF > 10
vars_to_remove_vif10 <- names(vif_full_16)[vif_full_16 > 10]
vars_to_remove_vif5 <- names(vif_full_16)[vif_full_16 > 5]

cat(sprintf("Variables with VIF > 10 (REMOVE): %d\n", length(vars_to_remove_vif10)))
if (length(vars_to_remove_vif10) > 0) {
  for (var in vars_to_remove_vif10) {
    cat(sprintf("  - %s (VIF = %.3f)\n", var, vif_full_16[var]))
  }
} else {
  cat("  (None)\n")
}
cat("\n")

cat(sprintf("Variables with VIF > 5 (CAUTION): %d\n", length(vars_to_remove_vif5)))
if (length(vars_to_remove_vif5) > 0) {
  for (var in vars_to_remove_vif5) {
    cat(sprintf("  - %s (VIF = %.3f)\n", var, vif_full_16[var]))
  }
} else {
  cat("  (None)\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Create VIF-only selected dataset
# Get VIF values <= 10, excluding NAs
vif_acceptable_names <- names(vif_full_16)[vif_full_16 <= 10 & !is.na(vif_full_16)]
# Only keep variables that actually exist in ext_cl
vars_keep_vif10 <- intersect(vif_acceptable_names, colnames(ext_cl))
ext_cl_vif_selected <- ext_cl %>% select(all_of(vars_keep_vif10))

cat(sprintf("VIF-ONLY Selection (VIF threshold = 10): %d variables\n", ncol(ext_cl_vif_selected)))
cat("Variables retained:\n")
print(colnames(ext_cl_vif_selected))
cat("\n")

# --- STEP 2: YOUR EXPERT SELECTION ---

cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("STEP 2: Your Expert Selection for Publication\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

# Your manual selection
ext_cl_red_pub <- ext_cl_red %>% 
  select(-contains("SalixHZM"), -contains("JuniperusHZM"), -contains("JulyT_Egel"))

your_selected_vars <- colnames(ext_cl_red_pub)

cat(sprintf("YOUR EXPERT SELECTION: %d variables\n", length(your_selected_vars)))
cat("Variables included:\n")
print(your_selected_vars)
cat("\n")

# --- STEP 3: COMPARISON ---

cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("STEP 3: Comparison - VIF Selection vs Your Expert Selection\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

vif_selected_vars <- colnames(ext_cl_vif_selected)

# Find overlap and differences
overlap <- intersect(vif_selected_vars, your_selected_vars)
removed_by_you_not_vif <- setdiff(your_selected_vars, vif_selected_vars)
removed_by_vif_not_you <- setdiff(vif_selected_vars, your_selected_vars)

cat(sprintf("✓ Variables in BOTH selections (overlap): %d\n", length(overlap)))
if (length(overlap) > 0) {
  cat("  ")
  print(overlap)
}
cat("\n")

cat(sprintf("🔍 Variables YOU removed but VIF would keep: %d\n", length(removed_by_you_not_vif)))
if (length(removed_by_you_not_vif) > 0) {
  for (var in removed_by_you_not_vif) {
    cat(sprintf("  - %s (VIF = %.3f)\n", var, vif_full_16[var]))
  }
  cat("  → You used expert knowledge to remove these despite acceptable VIFs\n")
} else {
  cat("  (None)\n")
}
cat("\n")

cat(sprintf("❌ Variables VIF would remove but YOU kept: %d\n", length(removed_by_vif_not_you)))
if (length(removed_by_vif_not_you) > 0) {
  for (var in removed_by_vif_not_you) {
    cat(sprintf("  - %s (VIF = %.3f)\n", var, vif_full_16[var]))
  }
  cat("  → VIF criterion would have removed these from analysis\n")
} else {
  cat("  (None)\n")
}
cat("\n")

# --- STEP 4: DETAILED COMPARISON TABLE ---

cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("Detailed Variable Comparison Table\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

comparison_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(vif_full_16),
  VIF = round(vif_full_16, 3),
  VIF_Status = ifelse(vif_full_16 > 10, "❌ Remove", 
                      ifelse(vif_full_16 > 5, "⚠️ Caution", "✓ OK")),
  VIF_Selected = names(vif_full_16) %in% vif_selected_vars,
  Your_Selected = names(vif_full_16) %in% your_selected_vars,
  Match = (names(vif_full_16) %in% vif_selected_vars) == (names(vif_full_16) %in% your_selected_vars)
)

kable(comparison_df, 
      caption = "Detailed Comparison: VIF-Based Selection vs Your Expert Selection",
      format = "html",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)

cat("\n\n")

# --- STEP 5: VALIDATION SUMMARY ---

cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("VALIDATION SUMMARY\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

agreement_rate <- length(overlap) / length(union(vif_selected_vars, your_selected_vars)) * 100

cat(sprintf("Selection size comparison:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  - VIF-only method:   %d variables\n", length(vif_selected_vars)))
cat(sprintf("  - Your selection:    %d variables\n", length(your_selected_vars)))
cat(sprintf("  - Agreement (overlap): %d variables (%.1f%% of union)\n", 
            length(overlap), agreement_rate))

cat("\n")

if (length(removed_by_vif_not_you) == 0 & length(removed_by_you_not_vif) == 0) {
  cat("✓ PERFECT MATCH: Your selection is identical to VIF-based selection!\n")
} else if (length(removed_by_vif_not_you) == 0) {
  cat("✓ EXCELLENT: Your selection includes all VIF-acceptable variables.\n")
  cat("  (You may have removed additional variables based on domain knowledge)\n")
} else if (length(removed_by_you_not_vif) == 0) {
  cat("⚠️  CAUTION: You kept variables that VIF would flag as problematic.\n")
  cat("  (This may be justified by ecological reasoning, but requires explanation)\n")
} else {
  cat("🔍 MIXED: Partial agreement with VIF criterion.\n")
  cat("  (Your expert knowledge diverges from statistical filtering)\n")
}

cat("\n\n")
```

```{r}
)

kable(vif_pig_pub_df, 
      caption = "Publication Model VIF Results - Your Expert Selection (Figure 1)",
      format = "html",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

vif_max_pig_pub <- max(vif_pig_pub, na.rm = TRUE)
vif_mean_pig_pub <- mean(vif_pig_pub, na.rm = TRUE)
vars_exceed_pig_pub <- sum(vif_pig_pub > VIF_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE)
vars_caution_pig_pub <- sum(vif_pig_pub > VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD & vif_pig_pub <= VIF_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("Summary for Publication Model (Your Expert Selection):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  - Starting dataset: 16 environmental variables\n"))
cat(sprintf("  - Your final selection: %d variables\n", length(vif_pig_pub)))
cat(sprintf("  - Maximum VIF in final model: %.3f\n", vif_max_pig_pub))
cat(sprintf("  - Mean VIF in final model: %.3f\n", vif_mean_pig_pub))
cat(sprintf("  - Variables exceeding threshold (>%g): %d\n", VIF_THRESHOLD, vars_exceed_pig_pub))
cat(sprintf("  - Variables in caution zone (>%g-%g): %d\n", VIF_CAUTION_THRESHOLD, VIF_THRESHOLD, vars_caution_pig_pub))
cat(sprintf("  - Assessment: %s\n", 
            ifelse(vars_exceed_pig_pub > 0, "❌ PROBLEMATIC", "✓ ACCEPTABLE")))
cat("  - Figure: RDA biplot shown in publication (RDA1: 27.9%, RDA2: 17.7%)\n\n")
```

# STEP 3: Generate Methods Text for Manuscript

## 3.1 Methods Section - Multicollinearity Assessment

```{r}
methods_text <- "

METHODS: Multicollinearity and Variable Selection
==================================================

Environmental Variables and Multicollinearity Screening
-------------------------------------------------------
Prior to Redundancy Analysis (RDA), environmental variables were screened for 
multicollinearity using variance inflation factors (VIF) computed via vif.cca() 
from the vegan package (Oksanen et al., 2022). Variance Inflation Factors measure 
how much the variance of a regression coefficient is inflated due to correlations 
with other predictor variables. Following standard paleoecological practice, we 
employed a VIF threshold of 10, meaning variables with VIF > 10 were flagged as 
exhibiting problematic multicollinearity.

Variables were systematically reduced through three stages:

1. Correlation-based pre-filtering: Environmental variables were first examined 
   for high correlations (r > 0.85) using correlation matrices and principal 
   component analysis (PCA). Highly correlated variable pairs were evaluated 
   (e.g., annual and July insolation), and the variable with lower ecological 
   relevance was removed. Similarly, redundant percentage-based variables 
   (e.g., arboreal pollen as a percentage of total pollen) were excluded in 
   favor of non-arboreal pollen (NAP).

2. VIF screening: Remaining environmental variables were tested for multicollinearity 
   using VIF analysis. All final models had maximum VIF values < 10, confirming 
   that multicollinearity was not problematic.

3. Data availability filtering: Variables that could not be interpolated across 
   the entire study interval (e.g., HZM pollen data ending at 13,258 cal yr BP) 
   were either excluded from full-dataset analyses or used in time-restricted 
   subsets (e.g., Bølling-Allerød-Younger Dryas period).

"

cat(methods_text)
```

## 3.2 Methods Section - RDA and Multiple Comparisons

```{r}
methods_rda <- "

Redundancy Analysis (RDA)
-------------------------
Redundancy Analysis was performed on primary producer community composition 
(pigments or diatoms as response variables) using the remaining environmental 
variables as predictors, all scaled to unit variance. The RDA models were fit 
using rda() from the vegan package (Oksanen et al., 2022) with centered 
responses (scale = TRUE).

Model Significance Testing
--------------------------
The significance of each full RDA model (constrained portion) was evaluated 
using permutation testing (999 permutations, unrestricted). Permutation tests 
assessed whether the combined explanatory power of all environmental variables 
was greater than expected by chance. This procedure tested the overall model fit 
but did not adjust individual variable contributions for multiple comparisons.

Important Caveat: Multiple Comparison Adjustment
-------------------------------------------------
While the overall RDA model significance was tested via permutation testing, 
the individual contributions of environmental variables were not subject to 
formal multiple-comparison correction (e.g., Bonferroni adjustment). This is 
a limitation acknowledged in recent paleoecological literature (Blanchet et al., 
2008). We partially mitigated this issue through:

1. Pre-filtering of variables based on correlation and VIF analysis, which 
   reduced the number of statistical tests from an initial pool of ~25 variables 
   to a final set of 10-19 variables (depending on the model).

2. Use of adjusted R² values to evaluate the explanatory power of the constrained 
   model rather than relying solely on permutation p-values.

3. Presentation of the full RDA output including site and species scores, allowing 
   readers to evaluate the practical significance of patterns independently of 
   p-values.

For more rigorous variable selection, future analyses could employ ordiR2step() 
with an adjusted R² stopping criterion (Blanchet et al., 2008), which provides 
automatic forward selection accounting for multiple testing.

"

cat(methods_rda)
```

## 3.3 Save Methods Text to File

```{r}
full_methods <- paste(methods_text, methods_rda, sep = "\n")

# Save to a text file for easy copying into manuscript
writeLines(full_methods, "../MANUSCRIPT_METHODS_RDA.txt")

cat("\n✓ Methods text saved to: ../MANUSCRIPT_METHODS_RDA.txt\n")
cat("  You can copy and paste this into your manuscript.\n\n")
```

```{r}
vif_interpretation <- data.frame(
  VIF_Range = c("1.0", "1.0 - 2.5", "2.5 - 5.0", "5.0 - 10.0", "> 10.0"),
  Interpretation = c(
    "No correlation with other variables",
    "Low correlation; acceptable",
    "Moderate correlation; acceptable",
    "High correlation; borderline problematic",
    "Very high correlation; remove variable"
  ),
  Action = c(
    "Keep variable",
    "Keep variable",
    "Keep variable",
    "Consider removing; check ecological relevance",
    "Remove variable (use in paleoecology)"
  )
)

kable(vif_interpretation,
      caption = "VIF Interpretation Guide",
      format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)
```
